reasons: The rule expects a transition/data-return clause in a hosting agreement; Section 4 as quoted addresses only notice, Termination Date and Termination Payment, and the rationale accounts for the survival clause (10.7) and confidentiality provisions containing no return obligation, so 'missing' is a supportable classification.

The inserted Section 4.3 is directionally correct for us as the customer: it obliges HDI (the host/vendor) to provide up to six months' transition assistance at its then-current rates, return Content, customer/user, and order data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certify deletion thereafter — tracking the model language and preferred position.

Placement is appropriate (appended in the termination section after the Termination Payment sub-clause) and numbering as a new 4.3 is consistent with the existing structure; drafting uses the contract's own defined terms (Company, HDI, Termination Date, Content, Site).
The comment is concise, first person plural, prefixed correctly, explains what changed and why, and offers the 90-day fallback, consistent with the tone guidance.
Deterministic checks pass and the added text is an insertion only, with no alteration of existing p0029 language — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.
